summary: createAiChatHandler reads a view context (what the user had open when sending the newest message) from the body field glirastesViewContext and gives it to the model as a data block. On by default; nothing sends the field yet, so an unchanged app sees no change.
howTo: Nothing to do. The browser side follows in a later release. To prepare: viewContext: false turns it off (null counts as not set); viewContext: { types, maxEntries, facts: { order: z.object({ status: z.string() }) } } narrows the accepted entity types (by default every type the request's tools declare with outputEntities / inputEntities), the entries per message and the facts kept (only for a type with a schema here). history must be 'none' for now; an invalid option throws when the handler is created. The runtime container passes no viewContext, so the default (on) applies there without an off switch until chat.viewContext. With piiShield the values are shielded like tool results. Only the built-in stream handler adds the block; continuations, guardrail-blocked requests, clarification answers, direct commands and a custom streamHandler get none; guardrails and hideIds do not see it.
